name: JB Pritzker
summary: JB Pritzker is a Democratic governor who has enacted a $15 minimum wage, cannabis legalization, abortion-rights and assault weapons laws, climate legislation and a graduated income tax proposal, while insisting on balanced budgets. He has been a prominent critic of the second Trump administration and of immigration enforcement tactics, while supporting deportation of violent offenders. He also backs nuclear expansion and housing deregulation.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Signed the law raising the Illinois minimum wage from $8.25 to $15 by 2025 and listed it among the things 'we did to help people' in his 2020 address.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Drove the 2020 Fair Tax amendment to replace the flat income tax with graduated rates, promising no increase at $250,000 or below and spending over $55 million on the campaign; his 2020 address calls for a 'fairer tax system'. No stated target for how much higher wealthy taxes should be.

unions-good.rationale: At the 2022 debate he backed the Workers' Rights Amendment, saying workers ought to be able to go in together for better wages, safer workplaces and benefits; his 2026 address recounts the Pullman strike and his record includes the Collective Bargaining Freedom Act.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Campaigned for the constitutional right to bargain collectively, saying 'That's what we're trying to guarantee' and arguing a single worker has far less power than a corporation.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Backed the Workers' Rights Amendment, which bars laws banning agreements that require union membership as a condition of employment; he did not himself speak to compulsory dues.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Proposed the Prescription Drug Affordability Act to rein in PBMs, backed a ban on junk fees and insurer rate justification, and said he would not sign a utility-written energy bill.

cut-welfare.rationale: Proposed raising TANF by $50 million and said the state must prioritise tackling poverty; he did not address the dependency claim itself.

limit-guns.rationale: Signed the 2023 assault weapons and high-capacity magazine ban, said it was done 'for all the victims', and at the DNC mocked open-carrying of AR-15s; the law limits certain weapons rather than ownership generally.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No recorded position found. (Reviewer: cannabis legalization is nearby evidence, not a view on recreational drugs generally.)

abortion-legal.rationale: Signed the Reproductive Health Act making abortion a fundamental right, expanded providers and removed copays, and told the legislature in 2023 he would not accept the loss of Roe for Illinois women.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Said in 2020 'We are obligated to make our future more equitable and fair' and that he is working to reverse harm done to communities left behind by discrimination; signed equity-centred cannabis law.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: 2019 executive order required schools to be affirming of transgender and non-binary students; in 2025 he named transgender people among groups being scapegoated. No statement on legal gender recognition specifically.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Said 'I will not join the chorus... eagerly look to slam shut an immigration door that was once open to our ancestors'; welcomed refugees. Backs removal of violent criminals only.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Criticised Trump's tariffs as taxes on working families and small businesses that raise prices and hurt farmers.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Said in 2020 'Urgent action is needed' on climate change and signed the Climate and Equitable Jobs Act with coal and gas phase-out dates.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Signed the act lifting Illinois's nuclear moratorium and issued a 2026 executive order to speed new reactors with a goal of at least two gigawatts.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Signed CEJA setting coal and gas plant phase-outs and sought to reduce carbon pollution; he did not discuss expanding extraction.

strong-leader.rationale: Stressed democratic guardrails and 'We don't have kings in America'; quoted Altgeld against presidential power to act at pleasure. Not a direct answer on gridlock.

separated-powers.rationale: Described annual addresses as bringing all branches together as 'guardrails of our democracy' and said power granted by voters is 'not unlimited'.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Said the power voters grant at each election 'is not unlimited' and that the only power the Constitution recognises is one capable of humbling itself before the people.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Promises and signs only balanced budgets, 'We have to live within our means', and criticises fiscal irresponsibility of past decades; did not address stimulus deficits at federal level.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Condemned right-wing 'censorship' of school libraries and book bans and said children should learn true history 'warts and all'.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Said he finds it difficult to resolve his feelings on the Skokie case protecting Nazi marches under the First Amendment while grateful for the community response; no clear position.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Condemned discrimination against immigrants, gay, lesbian and transgender people, women and minorities and called for equal justice, saying 'injustice' should not be bequeathed.

women-suffrage.rationale: Praised Illinois as first to ratify the amendment giving women the vote and quoted Altgeld that women deserve equal rewards and honours in every field.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Set diversity goals for public works and hiring, gave $10 million to minority-owned business expansion and defended diversity hiring against 'DEI hire' attacks.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Funded more state troopers, a new state police forensics lab and law enforcement support in budgets.

corporate-influence.rationale: Said special interests and large corporations extract money from everyday people, pushed ethics reform ending lobbying by legislators and refused a utility-written energy bill.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Called for rooting out 'greed and corruption in both parties' and said the well-connected work the system; did not generalise to all elites being out of touch.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Called to 'permanently eliminate the grocery tax' as 'one more regressive tax we just don't need' and did so.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Led the 2020 Fair Tax amendment to replace Illinois's flat income tax with graduated rates.

social-market-economy.rationale: Said Democrats want lower taxes, higher wages and business growth plus secure retirement and good health care, and pairs business recruitment with social programs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Created Team Illinois recruitment, EDGE incentives and a $100 million quantum computing partnership; no statement on directing investment as a principle.

state-harmful.rationale: Said 'only an idiot' would eliminate emergency response, clean air and water and other programmes and that Illinois suffered when government was gutted.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Proposes and defends expansive state roles in education, health care, child care and housing in every budget address.

taxation-theft.rationale: No recorded position found. (Reviewer: raising taxes is nearby evidence, not a view on whether taxation is theft.)

holocaust-denial.rationale: Helped build the Illinois Holocaust Museum and said he has spent time with survivors and knows the history intimately.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Listed gay and lesbian people among those who must not be discriminated against and flew a Pride flag over the capitol for the first time.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Said commitment to diversity and inclusion made 'our state is doing better because of it'.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Says 'I believe in building on what works', rejects 'magic bean fixes' and calls his approach 'pragmatic progressive'.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Said 'We don't have kings in America' and that power is 'not unlimited'; pledged not to defy courts.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Stressed constitutional limits on power and pledged 'We will not violate court orders... will not defy the Supreme Court'.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Wrote that the state fails everyone 'if we don't place a higher priority on tackling poverty'.

universal-healthcare.rationale: He explicitly proposes universal coverage beyond the Affordable Care Act.

public-ownership.rationale: He explicitly opposes government taking business equity and operating for private-sector profits.

empower-police-military.rationale: He personally expands State Police recruitment and resources alongside violence prevention.

decide-locally.rationale: For domestic Guard deployments he prioritizes local officials’ assessment over federal imposition.

rehabilitation.rationale: He advocates education, treatment and facilities supporting prisoners’ rehabilitation, while retaining punishment.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: His campaign explicitly defends marriage equality protections.

democracy-best.rationale: He defends slower democratic government despite disagreeable electoral outcomes.

ethnic-nation.rationale: His national account explicitly includes immigrants from around the world.

means-match-ends.rationale: Preserving democracy requires governing through democratic, rights-respecting methods.

state-as-business.rationale: He explicitly says government cannot operate like a profit-seeking business.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He supports Israel as a secure Jewish sanctuary alongside Palestinian statehood.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: He funds shelter, food and support for arriving noncitizens.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: He protects public libraries and expands their educational reach.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: He demands prosecution of federal agents who violated law.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

death-penalty.rationale: He explicitly answers no to restoring capital punishment.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: He endorses inclusive school sex education, consent and safety, retaining parental opt-outs.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: He says everyone, including wealthy people, bears responsibility for vulnerable families.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He explicitly identifies as a capitalist Democrat.

assisted-dying.rationale: He endorses physician-assisted dying for competent terminally ill adults under strict safeguards.

recognise-genocide.rationale: His formal proclamation recognizes the Armenian genocide.

family-wage.rationale: He rejects wages that cannot sustain a worker’s family.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: He personally expands earned-income and child tax credits.

no-business-privileges.rationale: He rejects special stadium subsidies while accepting ordinary business incentives and infrastructure.

notes:
Living person: answers rest only on his own words and measures he personally drove as governor; nothing inferred from party. Several cited reports quote him second-hand. Statements on Medicare for All and universal health care were left null because the only evidence is a second-hand paraphrase of an unverified transcript.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 24 answers taken from it, 30 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass; previous answers not consulted. One of ten priority statements answered; no inference for this living subject. Full active list and remaining nulls reviewed. Targeted searches found no attributable positions on Marxist historical causation, vanguardism, proletarian dictatorship, communal use-based land tenure or religion as illusion. His pro-enterprise language and criticism of abusive profiteering do not directly answer whether all ownership profit exploits workers. Religious affiliation, a papal visit, criticism of Bailey and disagreement with church teaching do not establish secular-school doctrine or general church–state separation. His own universal-coverage proposal is explicit in the new long interview. AI discussion supports safeguards and human oversight but not literal extinction priority, algorithmic civil government or acceleration despite disruption. Guard federalism is qualified to the domestic deployment context. Opposition to the Iran war does not establish universal nonintervention or defense-only warfare. Respect for Jewish refuge is combined with Palestinian statehood, not inferred historical territorial priority. Cannabis legalization does not establish legalization of every recreational drug. Prison failures are examined in the full interview and are not disguised as proven rehabilitative success; accountability rhetoric remains medium. Customer-service language is checked against his explicit rejection of running government for business profit. General food support does not answer replacing welfare with a negative income tax. No term-limit answer from simply running for reelection. No generic culture answers from personal family faith. No quiz-site estimates used.
